author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Six Flags Over Georgia ‘deeply saddened’ by tragedy, reportedly occurring on Goliath coaster with 175ft drop

One person has died and several others were injured in an incident involving a Six Flags rollercoaster on Monday afternoon in Georgia, according to police.

The incident took place a Six Flags Over Georgia, about 15 miles (25km) north-west of Atlanta, according to the Cobb county police department.

Continue reading...
title: One dead and more injured after incident on Six Flags rollercoaster in US

author: Ben Smee Queensland state correspondent
description:
Inmate advocacy group attacks watchdog’s ‘gutless retreat’ on Wacol youth remand centre

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Queensland ombudsman has backed away from calls to close a youth prison so “unsuitable” for children that some are self-harming in an attempt to get transferred, amid concerns that the Crisafulli government’s hardline bail laws could create a new crowding crisis in police watch houses.

The ombudsman, Anthony Reilly, published an inspection report last week that raised ser
title: Queensland prison where children self-harm to get transferred ‘more suitable’ than police watch-houses: ombudsman

author: Mollie Reilly
description:
Mitte, who played Walter White Jr on acclaimed show, had cerebral palsy and advocated for disability representation

The Breaking Bad actor RJ Mitte has died aged 34, his representatives confirmed on Monday.

“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” Mitte’s representatives said in a statement provided to Variety and Deadline.

Continue reading...
title: RJ Mitte, actor best known for Breaking Bad role, dies aged 34

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Sarah Hanson-Young is leading the Greens’ negotiations with the government over legislation designed to hold tech companies responsible for preventing harm to Australians, in particular children. The legislation is expected to be tabled in parliament this week.

Hanson-Young, the Greens’ manager of business in the Senate, said the party would wait to see the details of the legislation before deciding whether to support it. But the senator said the Greens supported the imperative, telling the ABC’s 7:30 program that big tech companies had been “running amok for far too long and we want laws that will actually hold them to account”.

Puttin
title: Australia politics live: Labor’s $630m funding boost for charities; Greens at odds about Ukraine weapons

author: Maya Yang in New York
description:
Several news outlets reported Blair allegedly punched a flight attendant, bit another and tried to open plane door

The actor Selma Blair was arrested on Sunday at John F Kennedy (JFK) airport in New York on allegations that she attacked flight attendants on a Delta Air Lines flight, according to officials.

Blair’s arrest happened at about 11am, after Port Authority of New York and New Jersey officials said they responded to a call “about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Air Lines flight 938 which was parked at the gate” at JFK after arriving from Los Angeles (LAX).

Continue reading...
title: Selma Blair arrested at JFK after she allegedly attacked flight attendants

author: Michael Savage Media editor
description:
Plans for a new theatre for world’s longest-running soap in Digbeth scrapped as part of cost-cutting measures

The BBC is set to stop recording The Archers in Birmingham for the first time in the show’s 75-year history, after scrapping plans for a radio drama theatre that was to be the new home of the world’s longest-running soap opera.

A pledge to move recordings to the so-called tea factory, the BBC’s new Birmingham hub in Digbeth, has become the latest victim of the corporation’s £500m cuts plan.

Continue reading...
title: BBC to stop recording The Archers in Birmingham for first time in its 75-year history

author: Rajeev Syal Home affairs editor
description:
Home secretary vows to defend against ‘threats from without and within that target our democracy’

Security arrangements for high-profile public figures including politicians and members of the royal family are to be urgently reviewed in the wake of the killing of Ann Widdecombe, Shabana Mahmood said on Monday.

The home secretary said former MPs, party leaders who are not MPs, peers, former members of devolved parliaments and party spokespeople will also be offered police support.

Continue reading...
title: Security for high-profile public figures to be reviewed after Ann Widdecombe’s murder

author: Maya Yang
description:
Top House Democrats question the ‘corrupt weaponization’ of federal government against Trump’s adversaries

Ilhan Omar’s Democratic colleagues have condemned federal agents’ search of the Minnesota congresswoman’s home on Monday morning, describing it as “deeply disturbing” and emblematic of the Trump administration’s “corrupt weaponization” of the US government.

House Democratic leaders, including minority leader Hakeem Jeffries, party whip Katherine Clark and caucus chair Pete Aguilar, issued a joint statement excoriating the president for the search.
title: Democrats rebuke federal raid of Ilhan Omar’s home: ‘rogue abuse of power’

author: Keely Aouga
description:
Runners in Moab 240 successfully evacuated from race route after flooding from remnants of tropical storm Rachel

About 70 runners participating in Utah’s Moab 240 ultramarathon were successfully evacuated from the race route on Sunday after being stranded by flooding stemming from the remnants of Tropical Storm Rachel.

The event’s host, Destination Trail, addressed the emergency rescue effort in a social media statement which confirmed that all runners were safe and accounted for.

Continue reading...
title: About 70 ultramarathon runners in Utah evacuated after being stranded by flooding

author: Dan Sabbagh
description:
UK to bring further sanctions against Tehran and IRGC after assessment Iran was likely to have coordinated incident

Andy Burnham said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps were “almost certainly” behind threats to RAF Fairford, the firmest attribution of responsibility made so far by the UK after an incident late last month.

The prime minister told MPs the UK would bring further sanctions against Tehran and the IRGC as a result, with more information to follow in an update from the home secretary, Shabana Mahmood.

Continue reading...
title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards ‘almost certainly’ behind RAF Fairford threats, says Burnham

author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
description:
Prime minister has reopened the debate over whether Russia did seek to influence the 2016 referendum

Andy Burnham unexpectedly reopened an old Brexit debate when he said he had been told after becoming prime minister that Russia had interfered in the 2016 EU referendum.

It was a contentious issue in the second half of the previous decade, but one that had largely been forgotten about as the UK finally adjusted to the reality of leaving the EU. Now Burnham’s comments have given the topic a fresh impetus.

Continue reading...
title: How significant are Burnham’s remarks on Kremlin interference in Brexit vote?

author: Andrew Pulver
description:
The revelation comes after the four-hour film’s Venice premiere drew a string of criticisms and insults from the founder of SpaceXAI

Alex Gibney, director of the new four-hour documentary about Elon Musk, said that Universal, owners of the film’s international distribution rights “wavered” over releasing the film outside North America.

Gibney was speaking to the New York Times as the film opened in the US (where it is being released by the independent distributor Bleecker Street), and appeared to confirm a story in the Hollywood Reporter that Universal, which had acquired the international rights to
title: Alex Gibney says Universal ‘wavered’ over releasing Elon Musk documentary

author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
Farage’s party says it would ‘embed’ immigration enforcement in UK and use ‘aerial imaging’ to identify people

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Children and mothers would not be exempt from plans by Reform UK to immediately deport 90,000 asylum seekers and impose a five-year ban on people being granted asylum.

The party’s most hardline immigration policies to date were condemned by refugee charities and others as “unworkable” and an abandonment of Britain’s tradition of helping victims of war after they were announced by Nigel Farage on Monday.

Continue reading...
title: Children and mothers included in Reform plan to immediately deport 90,000 asylum seekers

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Uneven caring responsibilities combined with a lack of flexible work options have prevented women from staying in senior positions, research suggests

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

More part-time bosses and “co-CEOs” could keep women in leadership and narrow Australia’s gender pay gap, the federal government’s Workplace Gender Equality Agency says.

WGEA warned resistance to gender equality was growing and urged employers to make management more flexible to reduce the gender pay gap, where women earn $0.79 for every $1 a man makes on average.

Continue read
title: More part-time bosses and co-CEOs could keep women in leadership and narrow Australia’s pay gap

author: Lisa Cox Environment and climate correspondent
description:
Environmental water to the area was halted after a complaint from a private landholder, leading to the deaths of wildlife and sheep

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Freshwater turtles rescued from a dried-up water hole in western New South Wales after the state government cut environmental water to the area are being returned home.

Late last month, 10 broad-shelled turtles and three Murray River turtles were released back into the Gingham water hole in the state’s Gwydir region.

Continue reading...
title: Rescued turtles return home after NSW government cut flows to wetland

author: Josh Taylor
description:
A history of tech giant legal challenges and US political criticism shows there’s no easy solution for the eSafety commissioner

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s online safety regulator has a few levers to limit the public seeing the US’s planned livestream of an execution, but history suggests it will lead to a very public fight.

The US defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, announced last week the planned execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan would be livestreamed when the military execution is carried out in early December.
title: Julie Inman Grant may be able to limit Australians seeing a livestreamed US execution – but it could start a diplomatic incident

author: Luca Ittimani and Catie McLeod
description:
Tenants encouraged to seek free options after online property platforms respond to Reserve Bank’s credit card payment reform

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Online property management platforms are charging renters new fees or pushing them on to paid “memberships” to avoid processing costs associated with card payments in the wake of the ban on surcharges.

Tenants have been encouraged to challenge or bypass additional fees charged by so-called rent-tech platforms, including in Victoria, where fees on rent payments are banned.

Continue reading...
title: Rent-tech platforms sidestepping credit card surcharge ban with new fees and paid ‘memberships’

author: Associated Press
description:
A businessman wanted in the US for allegedly bribing top Venezuelan officials has been taken into custody

A businessman wanted for years in the US for allegedly paying bribes to top Venezuelan officials in exchange for lucrative state contracts in Venezuela has been taken into custody.

Alvaro Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021 as part of an investigation into his longtime business partner, Alex Saab, a one-time ally of ousted Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro. The US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the state department had been offering a reward of up to $10m for information leading to his arrest.

Continue reading...
title: Fugitive businessman taken into US custody in Venezuela bribery case

author: Lorenzo Tondo
description:
Israeli PM calls for criminal investigation into soldiers and officers interviewed in Guardian-produced documentary

The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has ordered the country’s attorney general and the head of the Shin Bet security service to reveal the identities of soldiers and officers interviewed in the investigative documentary NAZA and prosecute them for causing “harm to Israel’s diplomatic and security interests”.

The award-winning documentary, directed by the Oscar-winning film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor and produced by the Guardian, details Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza. The film is in cinemas, including in the UK and the US, and will be shown in more than 50 countries.

Continue reading...
title: NAZA: Netanyahu orders identification and prosecution of film’s interviewees

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Energy minister says ‘fear has no place in the Saudi lexicon’ as paramilitary group again breach stretched defences

Saudi Arabia was forced to extend the suspension of all flights to and from its main international airport in Riyadh on Monday after a further round of Houthi missile attacks caused more damage and left one dead.

The Gulf nation said it was taking the step after Houthi missiles killed 13 people on Saturday and left more than 300 injured. Saudi state TV broadcast CCTV footage that showed passengers deluged in smoke and falling masonry as they queued at the airport terminal to board a plane just as the Houthi missile struck.
title: Saudi Arabia further suspends flights after latest deadly Houthi attack on airport

author: Martin Belam
description:
Ukrainian president says the deal is ‘news to me’ and that Russia is still attacking energy infrastructure. Plus, investigation into continuing mystery of Havana syndrome

Good morning. The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, has said it was “news to me” after Donald Trump announced a partial ceasefire deal in the Ukraine war. The US president had posted to social media to say: “Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed.”

There was no sign that the Kremlin was observing Trump’s ceasefire. According to Zelenskyy, Russian drones took to the sky “throughout the day” on Sunday and there were several airstrikes, including on energy infrastructure. He said Russia hit a power station in Kharkiv – the latest of more than 200 strikes during the past week against electricity generation and transm
title: Zelenskyy blindsided after Trump announces ‘energy ceasefire’ in Ukraine war | First Thing

author: Ed Walton and James Parrish for MetDesk
description:
Clear skies bring warm days and cold nights to Montenegro, while a low-pressure system moves towards Aegean Sea

  • Europe live – latest updates

Temperatures fluctuated dramatically in the Balkans last week, with unusually large differences between daytime highs and overnight lows – known as the diurnal range.

An area of high pressure over the region brought prolonged sunshine during the day, while clear skies at night allowed temperatures to drop rapidly as heat escaped into the atmosphere without cloud cover to slow the cooling.

Continue reading...
title: Balkan temperatures swing as heavy rain heads for Greece

author: Andrew Roth in Kyiv,  Jennifer Rankin in Brussels and Luke Harding
description:
Ukrainian president says at Warsaw summit Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ post, as Kyiv struck by Russian drones, ‘surprised’ him

  • Europe live – latest updates

Volodymyr Zelenskyy has vowed to respond to Russia’s continuing attacks on the Ukrainian power grid as European leaders rallied around Kyiv amid a feud with Donald Trump over Ukraine’s strikes on oil refineries.

Speaking to a gathering of European security officials in Warsaw on Monday, the Ukrainian president vowed to retaliate if strikes on Ukraine’s power grid continued: “If Russia does not agree to an energy ceasefire this winter, we will respond.”

Continue reading...
title: Zelenskyy vows to retaliate if Russian strikes on Ukraine’s power grid continue

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
Opinion piece by head of union Michael Slezak sparks disagreement with new ABC director of news, Simon Robinson

  • Sign up for Guardian Australia’s free weekly media newsletter here

ABC management has refused to rule out disciplinary action against a journalist and union office-holder for writing an opinion piece for the Australian Financial Review, according to the Media Entertainment and Arts Alliance (MEAA).

The award-winning ABC climate journalist, Michael Slezak, had an article published last week in Nine’s financial newspaper in his capacity as federal president of MEAA.
title: ABC reporter could face disciplinary action over opinion piece, journalists’ union says

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
The carnival is over for use of Australian band’s song they say was played without permission at conservative conference

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A member of legendary Australian band the Seekers has taken aim at a conference featuring Pauline Hanson for using a classic song, confirming no permission had been granted.

Bruce Woodley said the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) featured I Am Australian without approval, while the song’s co-author revealed Hanson had been previously threatened with legal action over its potential use.
title: ‘What planet is she on?’: the Seekers take aim at CPAC over use of I am Australian

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Coronial inquest begins into death of eight-year-old after 14 members of Toowoomba sect the Saints, including her parents, were found guilty of her manslaughter

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A medical specialist at the Queensland Children’s hospital warned that Elizabeth Struhs would not be safe at home with her mother years before her parents allowed her to die by withdrawing lifesaving medicine, a coronial inquest has heard.

Elizabeth, a type 1 diabetic, died at the age of eight from diabetic ketoacidosis on 7 January 2022, at her family home in Toowoomba, west of Brisbane, after her parents and other members of a religious sect withdrew the insulin she needed to survive and sat around singing and praying while s
title: Doctor warned Elizabeth Struhs would not be safe at home years before religious sect killed her by withdrawing medicine

author: Jillian Ambrose
description:
Calls for planned fuel duty rise to be scrapped as analysis finds average fuel bill could hit £1,965, up from £1,294

Millions of British van drivers face a combined £2.5bn cost to cover the rising price of diesel this year, according to figures, fuelling calls for the government to scrap its planned fuel duty rise.

The owners of diesel vans and pickups can expect to collectively spend almost £8.5bn at the pump this year, according to analysis for the Guardian, after diesel prices climbed to record highs due to a global fuel shortage caused by disruption to refineries in the Middle East and Russia.

Continue reading...
title: UK van drivers face extra £2.5bn in diesel costs this year, figures show

author: Aletha Adu Political correspondent
description:
Post-recess statement will focus on damage caused by Brexit and the need to cooperate on immigration and trade

Andy Burnham will put Brexit back on the Commons agenda as MPs return from recess, warning that failing to pursue a better deal with the EU would be a “major dereliction of duty”.

The prime minister will use a statement to the Commons on the first day back after the party conference break to urge MPs to face up to the damage caused by Brexit, and embrace closer ties with the EU to increase economic growth and tackle illegal immigration.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham to urge MPs to embrace closer ties with EU

author: Nino Bucci and Guardian staff
description:
MyCentre leader Samir Mohtadi, who also goes by Abu Hamza, refers to Islamic texts on the virtues of staying silent

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A leader of a Melbourne Islamic centre allegedly linked to the accused Flydubai hijacker has released a video extolling the virtues of staying silent, without directly commenting on the accusations from prosecutors in the United Arab Emirates.

Dr Hamad Saif al-Shamsi, the attorney general of the UAE, on the weekend said that investigators had
title: Melbourne Islamic leader silent on centre’s alleged Flydubai hijacker links in Facebook video

author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
description:
Thinktank’s influential pre-budget report urges key decisions to be made now and not put off until next year

John Healey has been warned by Britain’s leading tax and spending experts that his budget risks being a “work of fiction” unless he sets out plans to cover £35bn in spending pressures.

As the war in the Middle East rattles the public finances, the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) said the damage from higher inflation meant the chancellor would need to either top up funds for his current government spending plans or impose deep real-terms cuts by the end of the decade.

Continue reading...
title: IFS: budget will be ‘work of fiction’ without clear plan to cover UK spending pressures

author: Christopher Knaus
description:
Australian foreign minister welcomes Iraqi government’s decision to allow engineer to leave Baghdad

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian engineer Robert Pether has been allowed to leave Iraq after a four-year stint in a Baghdad jail cell that his family feared would kill him.

Pether’s family say they have been “living in hell” since he was arrested without charge in April 2021 in connection to a business dispute between his firm – which was building a new headquarters for the
title: Detained Australian engineer Robert Pether has left Iraq after being jailed in 2021

author: Josh Butler and Josh Taylor
description:
Federal government urged to prevent Australians from viewing planned broadcast of Fort Hood mass murderer Nidal Hasan’s execution

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

The Australian government should block the “barbaric” broadcast or live stream of a US military execution, Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young says, but it is unclear whether the commonwealth can or would be willing to do so.

While the communications department warned media broadcasters must “act responsibly” in reporting on
title: Australian Greens call for ‘barbaric’ US execution live stream to be blocked

author: Nick Visser
description:
Thunderstorms coupled with hot and dry conditions mean ‘fire danger is going to be right up today’, Rural Fire Service says

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A total fire ban is in place across greater Sydney, with temperatures forecast to reach 37C in the city’s west.

The Bureau of Meteorology said Sydney faced extreme fire danger due to hot, dry conditions and the chance of thunderstorms, with little rainfall.
title: Total fire ban for Sydney, with 37C temperatures and risk of bushfires from ‘dry lightning’
